title: Coco and Minty's Minty Mystery
markdown:
Coco the cockapoo and Minty the rabbit lived right next to the sunniest, happiest herb garden you ever did see. Sunshine felt like a warm hug. The breeze whispered tickly secrets through the leaves. And oh, the smells. Coco was a fluffy ball of energy with fur the colour of bright sunshine and one ear that did a funny little flop. His tail thump-thump-thumped against the soft crumbly earth when he did his super-duper zoomies. Minty, a tiny rabbit with fur like a fluffy cloud, had a nose that did a constant little wiggle-wiggle-wiggle. She loved to hop right behind Coco, her little pink feet barely making a sound. They were perfectly happy, perfectly sunny, and ready for smells.

Then, whoosh. A smell zipped past them. It was not a flower smell or a dirt smell. It was a minty smell, super fresh and super yummy, like a thousand tiny sparkly mint sweets doing a little dance. “Woof. Sniff sniff,” barked Coco, his floppy ear doing a little flip. His tail wagged so fast it looked like a furry propeller. “Ooooh, what’s that tickly whiff?” whispered Minty, her whiskers doing a little happy shimmy. The smell tickled their noses and made them feel bouncy. It was like a game of Follow the Scent had just begun, and it was the best game ever.

“It’s over here,” barked Coco, his happy bark bouncing around the garden. He bounced towards a big bushy plant that smelled a little like pine needles. But as soon as their noses got close, whoopsie-daisy, the minty smell seemed to giggle and float away, just out of reach. “Wait for me,” giggled Minty, her little feet thumping softly as she hopped after Coco. They found themselves near a patch of plants with leaves as soft and fuzzy as a baby lamb’s ear. “It’s over there now,” yipped Coco, doing a little somersault before chasing the disappearing scent. The sun was shining so brightly, making everything sparkle. They zigged and they zagged, they bounced and they hopped. Their tails and ears flopped and fluttered like happy flags. Coco agreed with a happy bark that sounded like yip-yip-hooray for minty smells. They were having such a fantastically fun chase, they did not even notice how the smell was leading them all the way to the very edge of the garden, right up to the little wooden fence that separated their garden from the wild meadow beyond. The breeze felt a little cooler here, carrying whispers from the other side.

With tiny tippy-toe steps they crept closer and closer to a big clump of tall leafy green plants. “It must be hiding here,” puffed Coco, his tail wagging with all the speed of a hummingbird’s wings. Minty peeked around a large heart-shaped leaf, her nose twitching. And guess what they saw? There was not a giant mint plant. No big round ball of minty-smelling goodness. Instead, a tiny gentle breeze was softly rustling through a patch of little delicate wild mint plants that were growing happily just on the other side of the fence. It was this tiny breeze, a whisper from the meadow, that was carrying the lovely minty smell all the way to them. It was not something they could hug or catch, but a sweet fresh message. “Oh,” said Coco, tilting his head. “It’s the wind sharing its secret.” “And the wild mint plants singing their fresh song,” squeaked Minty, her nose twitching with pure delight.

Coco gave a happy little wiggle-dance that shook his whole fluffy body, and Minty did a joyful hop-skip that ended with a little bounce. The chase itself had been the most fun part. They had bounced and sniffed and giggled and woofed and wiggled all through the sunny happy garden. Now they could both clearly smell the fresh wild mint that the gentle breeze was so kindly sharing with them. They sat by the fence a while, noses busy, one ear flopped, and let the mint come to them, which it did, over and over, as breezes will.
